entries.text: While filming his iconic disco scenes in Saturday Night Fever, Travolta had to switch between two identical suits because he sweated through each one so fast.
In 1991, Travolta married Kelly Preston twice — his first marriage with a Scientology minister was deemed illegal.
Travolta loves coffee so much that his morning routine involves making a single cup using a half pound of Starbucks Sumatra blend.

trueStory: All three are true. John Travolta is really sweaty, loves nuclear coffee, and is problematically Scientologisty.
fullText:
Truthsayer this week is focusing on the man, the myth, the fantastic dancer — John Travolta. 3 stories about John, 2 are false, 1 is true.

Truthsayer time.

#1 — John's breakthrough film role was Saturday Night Fever. While filming his iconic disco scenes, John had to switch between two copies of the same exact suit because he'd sweat through each one so fast. One would dry off while he was busy sweating up the other one.

#2 — In 1991, John married Kelly Preston. They actually had to get married twice due to the fact that his first marriage with a Scientology minister was deemed illegal.

#3 — John loves Coffee. In fact, he has said that his morning routine involves making a single cup of coffee using a half pound of Starbucks Sumatra blend.

Well, all three of these stories are true. John Travolta is really sweaty, loves nuclear coffee, and is problematically Scientologisty.

Here ends the Truthsayer.

topic: True story about Daniel Day-Lewis's preparation methods

entries.text: On the set of The Crucible in 1996, Lewis didn't bathe for the entire shoot to approximate 17th-century life.
For In the Name of the Father, where Daniel played a wrongly convicted prisoner, he spent 3 weeks inside a real prison in Northern Ireland.
On the set of There Will Be Blood, the cast had a big milkshake wrap party. Daniel Day-Lewis drank Paul Dano's milkshake. HE DRANK IT UP.

trueStory: Stinky Daniel Day-Lewis did not bathe while making The Crucible. It worked out OK — Daniel is still married to Arthur Miller's daughter Rebecca.
fullText:
OK — Daniel Day-Lewis is incredible. Part of the reason he is so good is due to the lengths he will go to get into character for every role he performs in Film. Here are 3 stories about his preparation methods for some famous roles — 2 stories are false, one is true.

Truthsayer time.

#1 — On the set of The Crucible in 1996, Lewis wanted to approximate what it would have been like to live in the 17th century, so he didn't bathe for the entire shoot.

#2 — For his role in the film In The Name Of The Father, where Daniel played a wrongly convicted prisoner, he spent 3 weeks inside a real prison in Northern Ireland.

#3 — On the set of There Will Be Blood, the cast and crew had a big milkshake party to wrap production. Daniel Day-Lewis drank Paul Dano's milkshake. HE DRANK IT UP.

So which one of those 3 stories about Daniel Day-Lewis is true?

It wasn't #2 — For In The Name Of The Father, Lewis had himself locked in solitary confinement in the abandoned prison where they were filming, keeping himself awake for three whole days — but did not spend time in Gen Pop.

It wasn't #3 — I could not confirm that there was a Milkshake party at the end of production for There Will Be Blood.

It was #1 — Stinky Daniel Day-Lewis did not bathe while making the film of Arthur Miller's The Crucible. It worked out OK though. Daniel is still married to Arthur Miller's daughter Rebecca.

Here ends the Truthsaying.

topic: True story about prototype jet-pack technology

entries.text: In 1966, Ohio inventor James Edmonds built his own Rocket Belt after seeing Thunderball, then veered off course and crashed into a local elementary school.
In the 90s, a company called JetGorge Explorers started testing jet packs to tour the Columbia River Gorge outside of Portland, before going bankrupt after spectacular crashes.

In the UK's Lake District, a tech startup called Gravity Industries has equipped paramedics with 1000 Horsepower Jet Suits to fly up and rescue injured climbers — arriving in 3 minutes vs 80 minutes on foot.

trueStory: Gravity Industries Jet Suits helping with UK Mountain Rescues. Go watch videos of these things — they are wild.
fullText:
To celebrate this incredible movie, The Rocketeer, here are 3 stories about prototype jet-pack technologies over the years — 2 of these stories are false, 1 is true.

Truthsaying time.

#1 — In 1966, after seeing the original Rocket Belt used in Thunderball, Ohio inventor James Edmonds started working on his own version in his garage. He was doing pretty well, until he veered off course and crashed into a local elementary school. He decided to try a different hobby after that.

#2 — In the 90s, a company called JetGorge Explorers started testing jet packs to tour the Columbia River Gorge outside of Portland. Their funding fell apart after a couple of spectacular crashes on test flights in the river, and the company went bankrupt.

#3 — In the UK's Lake District, a tech startup called Gravity Industries has equipped paramedics with 1000 Horsepower Jet Suits to fly up and rescue people who are injured or trapped while climbing. They had success helping a climber at the top of a mountain, arriving in 3 minutes rather than the 80 minutes it would take to hike up there.

In which of those 3 stories can you find the real Rocketeers?

It was #3 — Gravity Industries Jet Suits helping with UK Mountain Rescues. Go watch videos of these things, they are wild!

Here ends the Truthsaying.

topic: True story about Al Pacino's process

entries.text: While preparing to play a plain-clothes NYC policeman in Serpico, Pacino actually pulled over and threatened to arrest a truck driver for exhaust pollution.
Filming on Glengarry Glen Ross had to be suspended when Pacino went too far dressing down Kevin Spacey. Spacey took a swing at him and everyone jumped in.
While filming Ocean's Thirteen, Pacino staged a big dinner unveiling a new wine from his vineyard. Every beautiful bottle was filled with Boone's Farm. Matt Damon thought the wine was great.

trueStory: Pacino pulled a truck over while impersonating a plain-clothes police officer while getting ready to make Serpico.
fullText:
OK — Al Pacino — 64 feature films and counting. Some of these are wildly bad movies. Some are in the got damn pantheon, due in no small part to our short gravely king.

Here are 3 stories about Pacino's process — 2 are false, one is true.

Time for the Truthsaying.

#1 — While he was preparing to make Serpico, Pacino was so method getting ready to play a plain-clothes New York City policeman that he actually pulled over and threatened to arrest a truck driver for exhaust pollution.

#2 — Filming on Glengarry Glen Ross had to be suspended when Al got a little loose in the scene where he is dressing down Kevin Spacey. Spacey ended up taking a swing at him, and everyone jumped in before Pacino could tear him apart like a wolverine.

#3 — While filming Ocean's Thirteen, Pacino was tired of getting pranked by George Clooney. He staged a big dinner for the cast where he was unveiling a new wine from his vineyard. Every beautiful bottle was filled with Boone's Farm. Wild laughter ensued. Reportedly, Matt Damon thought the wine was great.

So, which of these 3 stories about Al Pacino is true?

It was #1 — Pacino pulled a truck over while impersonating a plain-clothes police officer while getting ready to make Serpico.

HooHa.

Here ends the Truthsaying.

topic: True story about the family history of an Inside Man star

entries.text: Denzel Washington was named after his father, who was named after his father's dentist and best friend, Dr. Frederick Denzel.
Christopher Plummer's great grandfather Sir John Abbot was a Prime Minister of England.
Jodie Foster and John Hinckley Jr — the man who attempted to assassinate Ronald Reagan to impress Jodie — are actually distant cousins.

trueStory: Jodie Foster and John Hinckley Jr are 9th cousins once removed. Denzel's name came from the doctor who delivered his father in 1909. Plummer's great grandfather Sir John Abbot was the third Prime Minister of Canada, not England.
closer: Families, amirite? Here ends the Truthsayer!
fullText:
OK, Truthsayer time for the Inside Man, and holy shit, what a cast. Here are 3 stories about the family histories of the principals in this movie — 2 stories are false, 1 is true.

Time for the Truthsayer.

#1 — Denzel Washington was named after his father, who in turn was named after HIS father's dentist and best friend, Dr. Frederick Denzel.

#2 — Christopher Plummer comes from a very notable family. In fact his great grandfather Sir John Abbot was a Prime Minister of England.

#3 — Jodie Foster was famously obsessed over by John Hinckley who attempted to assassinate Ronald Reagan to impress Jodie in 1981. Hinckley and Jodie are actually distant cousins.

OK — which story about the stars of Inside Man is true?

It wasn't #1 — Denzel's name came from the Doctor who delivered his father back in 1909 in Buckingham County, Virginia: Dr. Denzel.

It wasn't #2 — Christopher Plummer's great grandfather Sir John Abbot was actually the third Prime Minister of Canada.

It was the Jodie Foster story — she and John Hinckley Jr are 9th cousins once removed.

Families, amirite?

Here ends the Truthsayer!
